To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BLT1 and chemR23, two receptors for the specialized pro‐resoling mediator RvE1 are markedly upregulated in the AD brain, in regions that are associated with AD pathology, including the cingulate gyrum, the basal forebrain and the hippocampal region.
BLT1 and chemR23 are expressed at high levels in AD brains, and their levels are correlated with the density and severity of AD pathology.
BLT1 and the ChemR23 receptor are upregulated in AD brain and that their expression is correlated with the density and distribution of inflammation markers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression and distribution of the receptors for the S PMs RvE1 and LTB4 in AD and healthy controls.
the first description of the expression of BLT1 in neurons, and the first demonstration of the expression of ChemR23 in human brain.
the first demonstration of the distribution of BLTs and ChemR23s in human brain and their correlation with AD pathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BLT1 and chemR23 are increased in AD brain.
receptors for the SPSs RvE1 and LTB4 are increased in AD and that this may be an adaptive mechanism to promote resolution of inflammation in AD.
BLT1 and chemR23 are increased in AD brain and that the increase in these receptors correlates with inflammation and AD pathology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the levels of BLT1, ChemR23 and their ligands are increased in the AD brain.
the expression of BLT1, and to a lesser extent ChemR23, are upregulated in AD brain.
BLT1 and/or ChemR23 may be important for the resolution of AD pathology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BLT1 and chemR23 are expressed in neurons and glia in the human brain and are increased in AD, which may be a response to the chronic neuroinflammation.
BLT1 and/or ChemR23 are up‐regulated in the brains of AD patients and that the levels correlate with AD pathology.
BLT1 and chemR23 are expressed in the human brain in AD and that the levels of these receptors increase in parallel with AD‐associated inflammation.
